analysis.title: The Bottom Line: Markets shift from US politics to US inflation
key_insights: The October US CPI report, due 10 Nov, is the key macro event for markets in the coming week. It follows stronger-than-expected core inflation readings for both August and September, so it tests whether underlying price pressures remain elevated.

UniCredit forecasts October headline CPI at +0.3% mom and core CPI at +0.2% mom. Petrol prices were broadly unchanged in October and likely added little to headline CPI, unlike in September when energy gave a notable boost.
UniCredit expects year-on-year inflation to accelerate on base effects: headline CPI to 4.0% from 3.7% and core CPI to 2.8% from 2.6%.
Disinflation in core goods appears largely exhausted. Indirect effects from higher energy costs and AI-related supply bottlenecks offset the fading of tariff-related price pressures.

Shelter inflation should stay relatively benign, though the scope for further disinflation may be limited. Core services excluding housing is likely to remain sticky, partly because higher energy costs are passing through to travel-related categories such as airfare and lodging away from home.
UniCredit concludes that persistent services inflation and tentative signs that core goods disinflation is running out of steam are likely to keep the Fed firmly in tightening mode.

The IMF Global Markets Monitor, cited in the reading list, says the AI theme is entering a second phase in which value creation may shift from chipmakers and infrastructure providers to software platforms and companies that monetise AI adoption.
Recent UniCredit pieces listed include a 'dotcom era' comparison for the AI boom (31 Oct) and broadening market leadership (5 Nov). The summaries given for these are title-only.

risk_factors: Core goods disinflation may be exhausted, with energy pass-through and AI-related supply bottlenecks offsetting fading tariff effects.
Services inflation excluding housing is sticky, driven partly by higher energy costs passing through to travel categories.
Base effects push yoy headline CPI to 4.0%, and a hot print would reinforce the Fed's tightening bias.
geopolitical: Record attacks on shipping are keeping pre-war oil-market conditions out of sight (title of a 2 Nov UniCredit Market Spotlight).
US midterm elections have just taken place. The report's quote of the week is from President Trump: 'I wasn't on the ballot'. Related titles cover a 'blue tsunami' and the 'voting war'.
